periods.analysis: Harborview closed 2024-Q3 at 35 per 100k, comfortably under the <=45 target and in green status. With no prior quarter in this series, this is our baseline for the current respiratory and enteric disease monitoring cycle. The signal is consistent with strong vaccination uptake, timely school-nurse reporting, and steady follow-up by the North Shore and Bayside communicable disease teams. From a population-health perspective, the important point is not just that the rate is low, but that our prevention and early-notification systems are functioning before transmission accelerates.
periods.recommendations: Sustain weekly syndromic surveillance review with Harborview Regional Medical Center, the urgent-care network, and the 22-school nurse cohort. Extend the fall prevention push through the Marina Market and East Bluff library clinics, with emphasis on vaccination, hand hygiene, and staying home when symptomatic. Keep contact-tracing staffing at the current green-level posture, but preserve the ability to add per-diem investigators within 72 hours if clusters emerge.

periods.analysis: The rate rose to 43.2 per 100k in 2024-Q4, an increase of 8.2 from 35, but it remained green and below the <=45 target. This seasonal rise is expected as indoor gatherings, holiday travel, and school activities increase respiratory exposure. The case review team noted small linked clusters in two assisted-living facilities and one youth sports league, all managed without evidence of sustained community spread. We should read this as a normal winter pressure test, not as a loss of control.
periods.recommendations: Maintain the winter respiratory dashboard and continue twice-weekly line-list reconciliation with long-term care facilities through January. Send targeted prevention packets to assisted-living infection preventionists, youth sports coordinators, and large employers along the Route 6 corridor. Because the result is still green, extend the successful pop-up vaccination model to evening hours at the Civic Center annex rather than shifting to emergency operations.

periods.analysis: Harborview improved to 39.9 per 100k in 2025-Q1, down 3.3 from 43.2 and still green. That decline after the holiday quarter suggests that testing access, isolation guidance, and facility-level infection control kept winter transmission from widening. Our epidemiology unit closed the remaining long-term care cluster investigations and found no common-source exposure requiring broader public notification. The quarter shows prevention working at the system level: fewer secondary cases, faster reporting, and stable demand on outpatient partners.
periods.recommendations: Continue facility outreach, but step down assisted-living calls from twice weekly to weekly while keeping same-day escalation for new clusters. Sustain rapid electronic lab reporting audits with Harborview Regional and Seacoast Diagnostics so case interviews start within one business day. Use the Q1 improvement to refresh public messaging before spring break travel, focusing on symptom awareness and vaccination for high-risk residents.

periods.analysis: The rate fell to 33.9 per 100k in 2025-Q2, a decrease of 6 from 39.9, keeping Harborview solidly green. This is the clearest improvement in the arc so far and matches lower respiratory activity, better ventilation patterns, and strong school-based prevention before summer recess. The South Harbor mobile clinic completed 14 employer and community visits, which helped reach service workers who are less likely to use traditional appointment-based clinics. Lower incidence also gave staff time to complete chart cleanup and verify that case classifications were consistent across providers.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the South Harbor mobile clinic route through the ferry terminal, marina employers, and Westside food-service corridor at least twice monthly. Extend prevention work into summer camps by issuing a concise illness-exclusion and outbreak-reporting checklist to all permitted camp operators. Keep the dashboard public and plain-language, because low rates are when residents need reinforcement to maintain good habits rather than assume risk has disappeared.

periods.analysis: Harborview recorded 33.5 per 100k in 2025-Q3, down 0.4 from 33.9 and again green. The smaller quarter-over-quarter movement tells us the community is holding a low, stable baseline rather than seeing a temporary dip. Back-to-school surveillance through the Harborview School Health Collaborative did not identify unusual absenteeism or reportable disease clusters in the first six weeks of classes. This is the kind of steady performance we want before the higher-risk respiratory season begins.
periods.recommendations: Maintain school nurse reporting every Monday and add a short Thursday check-in during the first month after major holidays. Sustain low-barrier vaccination and testing access at the East Bluff, North Pier, and Civic Center sites, with bilingual materials for households new to Harborview. Use Q3 stability to pre-position PPE, specimen kits, and standing communication templates before winter demand rises.

periods.analysis: The rate increased to 41.7 per 100k in 2025-Q4, up 8.2 from 33.5, but remained green and below the <=45 target. This mirrors last year’s winter pattern and is consistent with colder weather, indoor events, and holiday travel through the harbor and regional rail station. The epidemiology review found several small household and workplace clusters, including at a Pier 3 logistics vendor, but no outbreak large enough to change the citywide risk posture. The increase deserves attention, but the system is absorbing it without crossing into yellow.
periods.recommendations: Keep the respiratory season incident rhythm at a watchful green level: weekly epidemiology briefings, rapid cluster huddles as needed, and no full EOC activation. Extend employer toolkits to the Pier 3 logistics firms, hospitality venues, and municipal worksites with reminders on paid sick leave practices and ventilation checks. Sustain the evening vaccine clinics through mid-January, especially for older adults and residents with chronic conditions.

periods.analysis: Harborview improved to 38.1 per 100k in 2026-Q1, down 3.6 from 41.7 and still green. The post-holiday decline is encouraging and shows that targeted winter measures helped blunt secondary transmission. Case investigators reported quicker interview completion after the January upgrade to the HView-ELR feed, particularly for lab results from Seacoast Diagnostics and urgent-care sites on Route 1A. The pattern is now familiar: a controlled winter rise followed by a measured decline, with prevention keeping us under target.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the HView-ELR quality checks for another quarter and publish a short provider bulletin on complete demographic and onset-date fields. Continue focused outreach to long-term care, shelters, and high-volume workplaces until respiratory activity returns to summer baseline. Begin planning the 2026 fall campaign now, using the Q4-to-Q1 experience to set clinic locations, staffing pools, and communications triggers.

periods.analysis: The rate declined to 31.2 per 100k in 2026-Q2, down 6.9 from 38.1 and the lowest value in this eight-quarter series. Harborview is well within green status, and the result reflects both seasonal easing and disciplined public health operations. The mobile outreach team completed spring vaccination and education stops at 11 senior housing properties, the ferry terminal, and three large food-processing employers without triggering any new cluster investigations. This closes the arc with a stronger baseline than where we began: 31.2 per 100k compared with 35 per 100k in 2024-Q3.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the prevention infrastructure that produced this low rate: mobile clinics, school reporting, provider data audits, and rapid cluster follow-up. Extend summer surveillance to include wastewater trend review at the North Outfall and Bayview treatment catchments as an early warning complement to reported cases. Use the low Q2 rate to train reserve investigators and refresh community partners, so Harborview enters the next respiratory season prepared rather than reactive.

periods.analysis: The 31.2 cases per 100,000 shown here is the carried-forward June rate, below the ceiling of 45. Without a new September surveillance extract, it cannot establish whether the favorable case rate persisted through the visitor season.
periods.recommendations: Reconcile provider and urgent-care reports with the September case extract, then assess the direction of the rate. Continue routine cluster follow-up and wastewater trend review.
